description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v4.0.0-alpha.19: the three own-account guards can now tell "we could not identify you" apart from "this is your own account" -- read UPGRADE.md section 32. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: SoftDeleteAsync, SetEnabledAsync and ToggleLockAsync refuse to act on the caller's own account, and since alpha.18 they also refuse when the caller's id cannot be resolved at all. That second refusal is correct and unchanged -- a SystemAdmin skips the permission gate entirely, so without it an unidentifiable caller could delete, disable or lock their own account unopposed -- but both branches raised the same message and the same MyIdentityErrorCodes.PermissionDenied. During the exact incident that fires the second one, a UserIdClaimType configured while old cookies are still in circulation, the UI asserted that the account being touched belongs to the operator when the truth is that the system could not identify the operator at all; and a consumer could not branch on the difference. The unresolved-id branch now raises the new MyIdentityErrorCodes.CallerIdentityUnresolved with a new describer message, CannotVerifyOwnAccount(); the genuine self-account refusal keeps PermissionDenied and its own message. If you catch on ErrorCode around those three calls, a catch that only looked at PermissionDenied stops seeing that case -- the case is not new, only its label. If you subclass MyIdentityMessageDescriber, override CannotVerifyOwnAccount() or that one message falls back to English; MyIdentityMessageDescriberAudit.FindUntranslated names it for you. Also: the synthetic principal produced inside RunAsSystemAsync now carries its id under the configured UserIdClaimType, and additionally as NameIdentifier when that knob is not the default, closing the last place where the accessor and alpha.18's user-id resolver could disagree. BREAKING: MyIdentitySystemAwareCurrentUserAccessor takes IOptions<IdentityOptions> as a second constructor argument -- source- and binary-breaking for code that constructs it directly rather than through DI; recompile, and outside DI pass Options.Create(new IdentityOptions()). Same shape as the break alpha.18 applied to the two IMyIdentityCurrentUserAccessor leaves, grouped into this alpha line on purpose because deferring it past stable 4.0 would have cost a major. API may still change before stable.
title: Kerberos.MyIdentity
